question: When evaluating a child with global developmental delay, thyroid function tests and serum phenylalanine should be included in the initial investigation work-up because congenital hypothyroidism and phenylketonuria are treatable causes that, if missed, lead to irreversible intellectual disability.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE. Congenital hypothyroidism and phenylketonuria are two of the most important treatable causes of developmental delay and intellectual disability. Both are included in India's RBSK newborn screening. In a child presenting with unexplained GDD, screening for these conditions is mandatory — missing them means a preventable disability is allowed to progress irreversibly.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Thyroid function tests (to detect congenital hypothyroidism) and metabolic screening including phenylalanine (to detect phenylketonuria) are among the most important investigations in a child with unexplained developmental delay because both are treatable causes included in India's Rashtriya Bal Swasthya Karyakram (RBSK) newborn screening programme. Early treatment prevents irreversible intellectual disability.
